context:
Design the phase contract first (w1) before writing any code. The phase model
must accommodate both the new post-measurement capture path (for PostgreSQL,
DuckDB, Redshift) and the existing inline/side-effect path (BigQuery, Spark).
Fix the thread-safety issue independently (w2) as it is a correctness bug
separate from the phase design. The orchestrator hook (w3) should be additive
— the inline capture in execute_query() can coexist until all adapters migrate.
description:
Plan capture is intended to run as a separate, isolated phase of the benchmark
— totally decoupled from the power/throughput measurement runs. The current
implementation does not match this intent: capture is wired inline inside each
adapter's execute_query() via the capture_plans flag, so EXPLAIN runs
interleaved with the timed measurement.

Two problems arise from inline capture:

1. Write isolation: even with a DML guard (see query-plan-capture-postgresql-dml-guard),
   the capture EXPLAIN executes inside the same transaction as the benchmark query.
   This exposes the measurement database state to a second round-trip, and for any
   platform where EXPLAIN ANALYZE re-executes (PostgreSQL, DuckDB with analyze_plans=True),
   the write runs twice unless actively guarded.

2. Measurement contamination: if capture EXPLAIN runs immediately after the timed
   query, it holds the connection open and may delay the next measured query. This
   affects throughput benchmarks with multiple concurrent streams.

The correct model: plan capture should be a separate benchmark phase that:
  - Runs after all power/throughput iterations complete (measurement already stable)
  - Uses a separate connection to avoid transaction interference
  - Issues EXPLAIN-only (no ANALYZE re-execution needed — structure from static plan)
  - Does not count toward any timing measurement

The phased model requires a dedicated "capture" phase hook in the run orchestrator
(benchbox/cli/commands/run.py) that is triggered by --capture-plans, distinct from
the --power and --throughput phases. The existing inline path can remain as a
compatibility layer for platforms that provide plans as a side effect of execution
(e.g., BigQuery job statistics, Spark event logs) where post-hoc capture is the
only option.

Secondary gap — thread safety of _plan_capture_iteration_counts:
benchbox/platforms/base/result_capture.py:323 initialises
`self._plan_capture_iteration_counts: dict[str, int] = {}` on the adapter instance.
Under concurrent stream execution (--streams > 1), multiple threads call
capture_query_plan() concurrently and mutate this dict without a lock. The dict
operations are CPython-GIL-protected for single-key reads/writes, but
plan_first_n filtering (lines 591-595) is a read-increment-write sequence that
can produce incorrect counts under preemption. This should be addressed as part
of the isolation architecture.

anti_patterns.dont: add ANALYZE to the capture-phase EXPLAIN call
anti_patterns.why: the phase is structural-plan-only; re-execution cost belongs in the measurement phase.

anti_patterns.dont: add the capture phase to the --throughput concurrent-stream path
anti_patterns.why: stream isolation is a pre-condition, not a deliverable of this TODO.

anti_patterns.dont: remove the inline capture from execute_query() in one shot
anti_patterns.why: BigQuery and Spark depend on it; migration is incremental.
plan_first_n is a global per-query-id counter, not per-thread.

preserves.behavior: DuckDB analyze_plans=False option must remain available for the capture phase.
Existing --capture-plans behavior must remain backward-compatible for SELECT-only benchmarks.
Platforms that capture plans as execution side effects (BigQuery job stats, Spark event logs) must continue to work — the inline path cannot be removed.
plan_fingerprints field in run metadata must continue to be populated.

Write a design note (inline in this TODO or as a brief ADR) covering:
  - Where in the run lifecycle the capture phase fires (after last power/throughput iteration)
  - Whether it uses the same adapter instance or a fresh connection
  - EXPLAIN options for capture-only mode (no ANALYZE — static plan structure only)

work_units.summary: Design the plan capture phase contract: inputs, outputs, timing, connection model

work_units.notes:
Replace the bare dict mutation at result_capture.py:591-595 with a
threading.Lock-protected increment. Options:
  a) Per-instance threading.Lock added to __init__ alongside the dict
  b) Replace dict with collections.Counter + lock
  c) Use threading.local() if per-thread isolation is preferred
Option (a) is simplest and consistent with the existing adapter-instance model.
Add a concurrent-stream unit test that fires capture_query_plan() from N
threads and asserts plan_first_n is honoured per-query_id (not per-thread).

Add a function to benchbox/cli/commands/run.py (or a new
benchbox/core/plan_capture_phase.py) that:
  - Accepts the list of query IDs and their SQL
  - Opens a fresh connection (to avoid contaminating measurement state)
  - Calls adapter.capture_query_plan(conn, sql, qid) with analyze_plans=False
    (structural plan only, no re-execution cost)
  - Collects results into a dict[str, QueryPlanDAG] keyed by query_id
  - Returns timing metadata (total capture time, per-query capture ms)
This is distinct from the inline capture path and is guarded by
--capture-plans + a "phase" flag (e.g., only fire when not in throughput
stream mode, or fire after all streams complete).
